stem: Navya rubs a plastic pen hard on a dry woollen scarf. Tiny paper bits jump onto the pen. She rubs a second identical plastic pen the same way so both pens gain like charges, then brings the two pens near each other.

parts.text: What happens when the two like-charged pens are brought near each other?

options.text: The two like-charged pens repel each other.
The two like-charged pens attract each other.
The pens attract paper bits only while they still touch the scarf.
The pens must be bar magnets because the paper bits moved.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Objects with like static charges repel; the pens were charged the same way, so they push apart.

teacher.key_rationale: Like static charges repel. Attraction of like charges reverses the rule; requiring contact with the scarf omits that charge can remain after rubbing; calling the pens magnets swaps the term.
